items.t: CME’s European Dairy Futures Launch Debuts to 126 Trades, Not ‘Strong’
sum: CME Group’s press release declared “strong” first-day trading for its new European dairy futures. The reality, visible in the exchange’s own figures, is a good deal thinner: 126 contracts changed hands.

CME Group (NASDAQ: CME) launched futures and options on European Butter, European Skimmed Milk Powder, European Whey Powder and European Liquid Milk on 23 November 2026, the first phase of a regional expansion that followed its September agreement with the European Energy Exchange (EEX) to take over EEX’s European dairy business. That part of the story holds up. What doesn’t hold up quite so well is the adjective CME chose to describe the result.

The 126 contracts and the resulting open interest of 60 – open interest being the number of contracts still outstanding at the end of the day, rather than closed out – belong to just two of the four products launched: Butter and Skimmed Milk Powder. CME’s own release discloses no volume figure at all for European Whey Powder or European Liquid Milk, a gap first flagged by TradingView. That’s not a rounding error in the release; it’s half the product line with nothing to show for day one.

Independent coverage reached for a more sober verdict than CME did. Securities.io described the launch as “modest initial participation” rather than anything resembling strength. For a brand-new contract with no established user base, a few hundred lots on day one isn’t unusual – plenty of successful futures contracts start small and build liquidity over months or years. But that’s a different claim from “strong”, and the distinction matters to anyone reading the headline rather than the fine print.

Context CME’s release doesn’t supply: the exchange’s own trading volume hit a firm-wide single-day record of 71,457,000 contracts on the very same day its dairy products launched, according to reporting on the company’s volume disclosures. Against that backdrop, 126 dairy contracts is a statistical footnote, not evidence of demand for the new product line. CME also reported a record October average daily volume of 30 million contracts, up 15% year-on-year, which only sharpens the contrast – this is a business where a single afternoon in the interest-rate or equity-index pits dwarfs an entire week of dairy trading.

sum: Jeeno Thitikul delivered another unforgettable performance Sunday at the 2026 CME Group Tour Championship in Naples, Florida. The Thai superstar captured her third consecutive championship at Tiburón Golf Club, completing another remarkable season. Thitikul fired a seven-under-par 65 during Sunday’s final round, finishing at 24-under-par for the tournament. Her performance secured a two-stroke victory over Japan’s Aki Iwai, who finished at 22-under-par.

Meanwhile, Nelly Korda finished third after another strong performance in the LPGA Tour’s season-ending event. However, nobody could match Thitikul’s impressive combination of power, precision, and putting throughout the final round. The victory earned Thitikul the tournament’s $4 million first-place prize. Furthermore, she surpassed Annika Sorenstam atop the LPGA Tour’s all-time career earnings list. Thitikul finished the tournament with 12 career LPGA Tour victories and another historic achievement on her résumé.

Thitikul entered Sunday’s final round at 17-under-par, one stroke behind overnight leader A Lim Kim. Yuri Yoshida also started the final round at 17-under, creating a competitive battle for the championship. Additionally, Korda remained within striking distance at 16-under-par. Several golfers had opportunities to capture the season’s biggest financial prize. However, Thitikul quickly demonstrated why she entered the tournament as the two-time defending champion.

She collected five birdies and an eagle during her final-round 65. Her aggressive approach helped separate her from a crowded leaderboard. Thitikul maintained her composure as challengers attempted to close the gap. More importantly, she avoided costly mistakes that could have changed the tournament’s outcome. Her ability to capitalize on scoring opportunities ultimately made the difference. The victory also extended her remarkable success at Tiburón Golf Club. Thitikul previously captured the championship in 2024 and 2025 before completing Sunday’s historic three-peat.
While Thitikul captured the championship, Aki Iwai delivered one of Sunday’s most impressive performances. The Japanese golfer fired a seven-under-par 65, matching the champion’s final-round score.

sum: A CME futures headline sent Bitcoin Cash soaring in September, and the coin has since surrendered every gain and then some. Buyers defended one price level before, and traders are now watching to see whether they will show up again.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Bitcoin Cash (CRYPTO:BCH) fell 14.6% this week, while Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) fell less, down just 3.3%. BCH is at $242.73, down 5.6% in 24 hours and below its lowest close in the previous 30 days, $249.42 on November 7.

BCH has also given back the surge that followed a futures announcement from CME Group (NASDAQ:CME | CME Price Prediction). The coin jumped 30% on that news, closing at $344.97 on September 22. Now BCH is down 59.5% this year and trades 93.6% below its all-time high of $3,785.82 from December 19, 2017. So why is BCH falling so much more than Bitcoin, and where might buyers step in?

In September, CME Group announced it would launch Bitcoin Cash futures, letting traders lock in a price now to buy or sell BCH later. The contracts began trading on October 19. Investors piled in on the news, but many started selling before the launch, a pattern known as “sell the news.”

BCH closed at $306.13 on September 30 and had dropped to $270.96 by October 8, well before the futures went live. The launch brought no fresh boost either. BCH closed at $275.98 on October 18, and its late-October closes ranged from $273.42 on October 29 to $295.76 on October 27.

Futures also give large traders a regulated way to short BCH, taking a position that profits when the price falls. CME said it added the contracts because of “strong client demand for institutional-grade risk management tools,” and managing risk often means hedging against a drop. That new two-way market, combined with fading excitement after the news, may explain why BCH keeps meeting selling pressure.

sum: Institutional traders are increasingly routing their XRP derivatives exposure through CME Group, a shift that is quietly redrawing the competitive map for the token's futures market even as spot prices wobble.

The migration toward the Chicago-based exchange operator signals that professional desks are favoring regulated infrastructure over crypto-native venues, according to CoinDesk. While the underlying research did not pin down specific share percentages, volume figures, or open-interest numbers, the directional change in venue mix carries its own significance for how the XRP derivatives complex is evolving.

CME's growing presence in XRP futures comes at a moment when the broader crypto market is pulling back. Yet futures exposure on the exchange has continued to climb, a divergence that puts institutional positioning squarely in focus for traders trying to read how regulated derivatives behave during risk-off stretches.

Market share in XRP futures refers to the portion of total derivatives activity clearing on a given venue, not the raw size of the XRP market. A venue can gain share while overall activity stays flat, because the metric describes distribution across exchanges rather than absolute growth.

That distinction separates three commonly conflated readings: volume captures turnover over a period, open interest captures outstanding contracts at a point in time, and share measures the split between venues. The structural signal here comes from the venue mix, not from XRP price action itself.

CME has steadily built out its XRP franchise over the past year. The exchange launched Solana and XRP futures options, saw XRP futures open interest cross the $1 billion threshold, and has continued expanding its digital-asset lineup with new listings and plans for Nasdaq CME crypto index futures. A stronger XRP presence extends that push beyond bitcoin and ether into altcoin derivatives coverage.

CME operates as a regulated futures venue, and its large-trader positioning is reported through CFTC commitment data. Institutional desks typically favor exchanges that fit existing risk-management, custody, and compliance frameworks, which is one plausible reason XRP exposure would migrate there.
